notes.title: Mountain Clans Stalwart Defenders of the Peaks
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/4687931d6f5e4e4238d358079ddfdcd212adb4c8.png[/img]
Determined and strong-willed dwarves from the tops of the frosty mountains, who have experienced both the terrifying cold of the most remote peaks and the frightening darkness of ancient tunnels. Dwarves are distinguished by their well-developed musculature, thick beards, fighting temperament, and short stature. But rest assured, even the centuries-old elves of the Forest Alliance do not look down on this people.

We recommend that you don't underestimate these guys either! They lack speed and initiative, but health, defense, buffs and many other features of this formation more than compensate for all their shortcomings.

Let's consider the features of the representatives of the different classes of this faction, and finish with non-obvious, but very useful chips.

The starting dwarf mage, the hermit, already has options to deal aoe damage and slow down opponents. This helps you not only effectively control the battlefield, but also level up someone else's speed advantage. At rank two, you are free to choose between enhanced deceleration and strong earth elementals, or opt for area damage and summoning a water elemental, a useful and mobile healer.

Healers do not have as powerful healing as the priests of the Free Empire, but each healing ability of dwarven herbalists and alchemists boosts the healed person's defenses, increasing the effectiveness of their health. A very useful option to remove negative effects appears at rank two. Necessary if the enemy has a lot of damage with poison, bleeding or has armor piercing.

The trappers of the Mountain Clans have a unique trap mechanic at the moment. A trapper can set a trap that when activated triggers sector damage or aoe damage. With proper positioning, you can easily move your opponent to the trap and turn the tide of battle... Or you can place a wounded unit on the trap yourself to bury a couple of your opponent's units with it.

Riflemen, Warriors and Leaders have an important common feature - “ Hird”. If these units are adjacent to each other, they all get defense boosts. If your opponent has no aoe damage or your mages have run out of aoe abilities, then you just have to put an artifact as a leader and stand your warrior, gunner and leader around it. Hardly anyone will be able to make your ranks shake. The archers themselves have a variety of skills: armor piercing and multi-attack are already on the first rank, and on the second rank you can both annoy the enemy by applying bleeding and make remote repulsion or attraction attacks.

Leaders can offer you the option of installing artifacts not only for defense and attack bonuses, but also for regeneration, making the Dwarf formation able to compete with humans in survivability. At rank two, you may prefer the Skald to the Jarl. He's not as strong and powerful as the last one, but he can give a defense buff to all allies on the battlefield at once, making positioning easier for your squad.

Dwarf warriors are strong and adaptive - thanks to their repulsion strike, they can easily combine with both trap catchers and mages of any formation. And at rank two, you're offered the classic choice between survivability and damage. Shilder won't let even a jumpy elf get past him, and Berserk will easily chew a hole in the enemy's defense with his axes.

Finally, and most importantly. If you noticed, the Mountain Clans have a passive skill called “Mountaineers”. They spend 1 OP instead of 2 to stand on an elevated sector, and they gain defense buffs when they occupy such a sector. Each holding point in the eponymous mode is an elevation. Stand a Hird warrior on such a point, press “Battle Formation”, place a defense artifact next to it and watch your opponent try to kill it during the whole battle.

notes.title: Mastering the Forest Alliance
notes.content:
Graceful and deadly elves, blessed with the gift of long centuries of life and an alliance with some of the oldest inhabitants of the world of Odra, the children of the evergreen forests of Krong. Too noble to seem dangerous, elves are capable of punishing anyone who underestimates their power.

Elves can be considered one of the most difficult factions to master. As they say: “Easy to learn, hard to master”. The whole point is that elves are characterized by the weakest survivability of all the formations, but they compensate for it with high damage and incredible mobility. But the main difficulty lies not in realizing the advantage of elves before they lose health, but in activating their passive effects.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/7ef95d76e998a561c5127b8035e9f9a5662a1a8a.png[/img]
Every unit in the Forest Alliance has a passive feature called “Children of Krong”. It gives the units of the formation 10% to all defense parameters if they stand on a sector with the Forest Cover effect. These sectors do not slow them down, which is not the case for all other formations. This effect is due to the special mechanics of the faction, which we will talk about later. But we already note that elves are more dependent on synergies between units of their faction.

Elven mages differ from all others in their stable and effective area damage. Their aoe damage can also be used as battlefield control, as area damage is periodic, over several rounds. If you use Poison Cloud on an enemy's power spot or hold sector, you're almost guaranteed to chase them away or deal a lot of damage. With mages of the second rank the situation is more interesting. You can either use an Archon with enhanced poison damage and the ability to aoe downgrade enemy armor, or you can choose to use an Oracle Summoner, who can summon nature elementals and create vegetation, which is the most important passive of the Forest Alliance.

Forest Union healers have two healing options: normal and enhanced. The latter only works on sectors with vegetation. At rank 2, you can either maximize both heals into a single target, or get a massive hit, negative effect removal, or even healing with a bonus to attack power in your arsenal. Choose what suits your play style best.

Elven arrows are the easiest to learn and use. Difficulties abound in using the other classes. Elven shooters have truly eagle vision, so they are able to hit targets at a longer range using the “Aiming Shot” ability. There are also multi-attacks in their arsenal. Second rank units allow you to get either increased damage and bleeding effects at long range with Marauders, or less damage but better control of the battlefield with the Krong Sentry's Repulsion Shot.

Krong Sentry are the only archers who share the passive feature “Krong Guardians” with all Forest Union warriors. Elves are a proud and independent people, so the passive is activated only when units are in the thicket and only if there is no other ally in the neighboring sector. Thus, the units can get a very solid bonus to attack, which can turn them into real killing machines. Elven warriors have excellent mobility thanks to their jerks and the ability to deal splash damage. At rank two you may prefer the more armored koppers, the Krong Guards, which can push back opponents and hit two opponents through and bleed them both!

That left the agile players and leaders to take on the burden of the most difficult synergy in the formation, or even the entire game. The first and second ranked leaders, Ents and Huorns, are able to plant seeds that create the very vegetation mentioned at the beginning of this article, Forest Cover. As the seed grows, the cover turns into a Krongha Forest, greatly enhancing all the bonuses of the units standing on the cells. Huorn also has the same feature as warriors. As a guardian of the Krong, he gets an even greater bonus when standing in vegetation with no units nearby! Nymphs and Dryads, first and second ranked agility players, can use vegetation sectors for invisibility. The latter also have the Symbiosis ability, which multiplies their survivability in the forest sector. The Forest Union also has its own boost for the whole team - just use “Call of the Ents” with your Huorn.

We haven't forgotten about Undines and Dark Gworns either. Grim inhabitants of the swamps, brutally killing anyone who accidentally wanders into the swamps. And the features of these creepy units are corresponding. Dark Gworn plants a tainted seed that grows into a gloomy tree, spreading swamp cells around that he and Undine can use. Not only do swamp sectors significantly lower the attack and defense of all units standing on them (except Gworn and Undine, of course), but they also give swamp dwellers the ability to poison enemies when attacking. Undine is able not only to use invisibility in the swamp, but also to teleport from one desecrated sector to another. However, there is a price to pay for such power: swamp sectors weaken allies as well, and the characteristics of these two are lower than those of their “kinder brethren”.

And this is not all the features of the faction. By no means neglect the elves. In skillful hands it is a real weapon.

notes.title: Understanding Defense and Resistances
Mastering Positioning for Victory in Odra Online
notes.content:
Positioning in games can depend on different factors: the presence of obstacles, the enemy's ability to deal mass damage, the number and types of units, their defensive and attack performance, unit abilities and many others... In this article we will tell you, dear players, about the importance of positioning in Odra Online. Believe me, once you have mastered the art of positioning, you will be able to achieve victory where it seems impossible.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/99ebaf33b205af3022040d9eac9dceef87596102.png[/img]
Let's briefly mention some basic rules, although they will seem obvious to many people. First of all, Warriors and Leaders should be in the vanguard of your army, and Riflemen behind. Mages, because of their low mobility, should be kept somewhere in the center. But it is better to start the battle as close to the enemy army as possible. Taking into account the arc-shape of the unit placement area, you should place the Mage closer to one of the edges. But it is better not to follow this rule if you are playing Harvest, because then it will be too easy for the neutral units to get to your Mage and ruin your game.  Another tip is to keep your units farther apart if your opponent has a Mage in his arsenal. If you have a Forest Union unit, keep your units spread out even if your opponent doesn't have AoE damage.

Another aspect of the game that you definitely need to consider when positioning is Free Attacks. It makes sense to keep Warriors and Leaders at a small distance from each other, but so that they can move towards each other or so that at least half of them can reach the buff from the artifact (banner). This will allow the characters not to lose in bonuses to characteristics and have the largest “radius of control” - the area of cells, when trying to cross which the enemy will be able to attack. Remember, too, that Dodgers are able to ignore free attacks. Then at least one of your Warriors, if you spread them out evenly, will be able to turn around and overtake him to protect your rearguard (Mages and Riflemen) from catastrophic damage.

Now let's touch on the principle of damage dealing. It's very simple and applies to all classes. Damage from abilities is constant and does not depend on any positioning modifiers. But the damage of normal attacks - even more so. When attacking from the front, no crystals are lit up on the attack indicator - this means that the standard damage, X, will be dealt. When attacking from the side, one crystal is lit up on the indicator. In this case we get increased damage, 1.2X. And how can we do without backstabs? They deal one and a half times more damage, and both crystals light up on the indicator.

The interesting thing is that these rules work for every attack, even ranged attacks. Ranged attacks have another positioning modifier that affects the final damage. So as not to confuse you, let's label both point by point:
[list]
[*] Range - the number of sectors from the Rifleman/Mage to the target.
[*] Obstacles - presence of other units in the direction of the planned attack.
[/list]If the arrow/mage's nndicator is not spinning - the attack damage is reduced by 50% of the attack power. This means that either there is an obstacle on the way to the target, or it is too far away to deal damage effectively.

If the arrow/staff is displayed broken, it indicates that the attack power for this strike is reduced by 75% and that both conditions are met: the enemy is far away and there are other units on the way to it.

The ideal attack is an attack whose indicator looks like a whole spinning staff or a whole spinning arrow.

One last piece of advice - watch not only the positioning of your units, but also in which direction they are turned. If you have movement points to get off the current square and take it again, changing the direction of the turn - do it. It will help avoid quite a few problems. But be careful - the author, following this advice, left a Hold Point and couldn't get back up because it requires 2 movement points, not 1.

notes.title: Strategic Moves - The Power of Block and Wait
notes.content:
We are glad to welcome you and thank you in advance for your time! This time our message will be brief, but at the same time quite important.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/6b1c2652350ce2d12b2a547e88d7b54312de9964.jpg[/img] 
As you may have noticed, next to the “End turn” button there are two more interesting options, the usefulness of which may not be clear right away. The “Block” button is pretty self-explanatory - instead of taking an attacking action (most often at the moment when he can't attack the enemy), the character stands in a defensive stance and gets resistance boosts. The block can be used in many different ways, and I'm sure you'll have no problem naming at least two uses of this option.

But what about the “Wait” button? At first glance, the character simply skips a turn and gets nothing in return. It may seem that this option is for giving in to your opponent, but that's not the case. A skillful player is able to use Waiting in a way that can turn the outcome of a battle around.

The thing is that this option doesn't skip a unit's turn, it puts it at the end of the round. You can move a unit by spending movement points, but you can't attack it by using Waiting. Then you can continue your unit's move at the end of the round without losing the OD you have saved.

If you use “Wait” with a unit with a high initiative level (an archer or wizard, for example), you can essentially move twice: at the end of the current turn and at the beginning of the current turn. Let's say it's your crossbowman's turn. He has a repulsion shot, but there is no one to use it on. You see that an enemy unit can move to a place of strength or stand next to your warrior or leader. You press “Wait” and at the end of the turn you push the enemy unit away from the place of strength. If the pushed unit was standing next to your warrior or leader with a free attack ability, it gets a hit in return.

And that's just one of many options. Don't be afraid to experiment, and you'll get some pretty spectacular victories.

notes.title: Battle Pits is a Test of Endurance and Strategy
notes.content:
Odra Online currently features three unique game modes: Confrontation, Harvest, and Holdout. That's what a person who hasn't had time to appreciate all that the game has to offer at the moment would say. In fact, there are four such modes. And about the last of them, but not in terms of importance and even more uniqueness, we will now tell you.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/23eedb71cd66c520f59abed992418e0f665c359b.jpg[/img]
Battle Pits - a special PvE-mode, in which the player has to take control of his squad, which must repel progressively arriving waves of enemies, including units with high levels, and units of higher 2nd rank, and even mini-bosses, which except for Battle Pits can be found now only in Harvest.

One of the important advantages of this mode is that it is not secondary in any possible sense. Battle Pits has its own ranking table with opportunities to win rewards at the end of the season, there is a separate table for paired games with other rewards. Yes, you have the opportunity to crush AI (we should note, bots in the game should not be underestimated) together with your partner now. Agree with your buddy, show your skills together and climb to the top - what could be better?

Fighting pits are divided into stages, which change in the game every 10 rounds, if by the time the 11th round starts all the opponents of the previous stage have already been defeated. Places of Power appear during the game according to the standard rules and are activated on the third round after their appearance. Thanks to them you can maintain your units' resource reserves during the whole race - you can convert the whole squad into 2nd rank units, heal wounded fighters, restore the number of skills. And sometimes it will be extremely useful to finish a mini-boss with “Deathstroke”. Similar to “Harvest”, every few rounds 3-4 enemy units enter the arena with the probability of a mini-boss of the same rank as the units that entered the arena. In case of an early victory over all stage opponents, you have time to prepare - take positions, heal units with healers and Strength Points, and recover.

“Why is it possible to select a stage in the Battle Pits game menu if they change already in the game?” - you ask... It's all about your ranked progress being saved. Let's say you've been frantically pumping your units for months and you've checked out the Battle Pits to conquer them here and now. You made it to stage 4 and lost, scoring 670 points. The author of this article, at least, mastered this mode this way.

This means that now you can start from stage 1 to stage 4 with the specified number of points. If it's stage 4, you start with 600 points as if you had accumulated them from scratch from stage 1, but it's not that simple. For one thing, the power level of your opponents grows with each stage. If on stage 1 you face units of rank 1 “Champion” level, on stage 2 it will be “Elite”. On the 3rd, it's 2nd rank Champion level units, and on the 4th, it's already Elite. It seems more profitable to start over to have time to convert all units and accumulate power points? On the one hand, yes.

We won't tell you and bore you with numbers, but we'll note that the number of strength points and even the rank of the units you can place varies at different stages. The main thing is to reach the necessary stages. In addition, starting from the last stage ensures that all your units have full health bars and ability pools.

notes.title: The Secrets of Odra Arenas
notes.content:
[p]
Once again we welcome you, dear players. Now we would like to talk to you about our arenas and their peculiarities. We are sure that you have already noticed some regularities and differences between the battlefields. Be sure to tell us if there is something we left out in this article.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/4573d58319e01d3907df506cc2c5197d733ef01c.png"][/img][/p][p]Arenas have three levels: 
[/p][list][*][p] Beginner;
[/p][/*][*][p] Champion;
[/p][/*][*][p] Master.
[/p][/*][/list][p]Let's break down their differences. Firstly, the strength of neutral units: bot units, elementals that appeared on the force locations and units in the Harvest mode. On “Beginner” difficulty, the elementals from Force Places and Harvest units are “Veteran” level, and minibosses do not appear in Harvest. Bot units, however, are of standard rank. On the “Champion” and “Master” difficulties, things are much simpler - units have “Champion” and “Elite” ranks, respectively. Minibosses on “Champion” in Harvest appear with a good chance, but on “Master” they are mandatory.

The regularities of other elements of the arena are a bit more difficult to follow, even though the game gives hints. These are traps and towers. Towers, it should be noted, only work in the classic mode, in Confrontation. They are activated from the 8th round. Each round their damage increases, on the “Champion” difficulty they have double the base damage, and on the “Master” difficulty - triple. Not an obvious point at all - the first tower always attacks the unit of the player who moves first in the round. Understanding how turrets work can be very useful - if you have one tank or mobile unit left in your arsenal with more health than your opponent's units, but it will lose to them in a direct skirmish - avoid damage and wait for the turrets to win the fight for you. This is a good strategy if you're left with a single unarmored unit with full health and the enemy is firing from a distance.

We won't reveal the secret of traps, but we will note that the base damage of traps is twice as high on “Champion” and three times as high on “Master”. On these difficulties, there is a possibility of fire traps that deal the appropriate type of damage and burn sector effects.

To finish with a small fact - arena traps activate on their own, so they pose a threat even to agile players.
[/p]

notes.title: The Battlefields of Odra Online: Explore Diverse and Strategic Arenas
notes.content:
Are your warriors already trampling the battlefields of Odra Online? Spilling the blood of enemies in the name of your glory and ranking advancement? We're sure they are. And if so, you've probably noticed some peculiarities of our arenas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/a41491cabb80b05d4de9745275cfff88ec3830b6.png[/img]

We will talk about the technical details of arenas that affect your gameplay a bit later. In this post we would like to draw your attention to the visual diversity.

There are more than 90 different arenas in Odra Online. Not all of them appear with equal chance because many of them depend on the rules of combat set by the game (or by you). For example, the game map in Confrontation and Harvest modes will be different visually, as the map with towers and the map without them are different maps. The same goes for Holdout, which is technically distinguished by the presence of Holdout sectors. We won't disclose how many maps of all the prepared maps are for each of the modes, but we assure you that there are plenty. If you get the same ones in the rating - most likely, today you are just unlucky. But, actively and long playing our game, you will definitely familiarize yourself with all the current arenas.

Another criterion for the appearance of the arena is its difficulty. This is the parameter responsible for the type of damage of traps, damage of traps and towers (in Confrontation), the level of hostile elementals, the level of bots and the level of hostile units in Harvest. A lot of things are responsible for, but now you know that the difficulty of arenas also determines how the arena will look.

In the future there are many plans to expand the diversity of arenas - we will experiment with the size and geometry of maps, indestructible obstacles and much more. As always, you can share your thoughts on this in the comments. Be sure to stay tuned to discover the world of Odra together!

Below we have attached our favorite screenshots of some of the available arenas:

notes.title: Mastering Holdout Mode: Strategies for Dominance
notes.content:
Standing guard over Holdpoints in the eponymous mode, Heirs? Great, and we're standing guard over your comfort in our game. It's not hard to guess that today we're going to share with you the tricks of the Hold mode.

For those who have not yet understood the game modes and do not want to waste time searching for the appropriate post, let us make it clear. “Holdout” is one of three Odra Online modes that offer fundamentally different victory conditions. What's more, in this sense, “Holdout” stands out both against the standard Confrontation and the unpredictable “Harvest”. During the game it is necessary to hold for a certain period of time the designated sectors called Holding Points. Their number depends on the number of players. If there are two of you, one point will appear closer to each of you and one in the center. That makes three dots. If there are three of you, then by the same logic there will be four.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/61c2243496544b9fc9b859f5b7bb59c2d0b814ee.png[/img]

All battles with the “Hold” mode go for ten rounds. there is no possibility to win before the end of the tenth round, but this victory can be guaranteed. Even after the loss of all units of one side, the game will continue until the end of the specified number of rounds. If you, for example, have earned 80 Retention points by occupying most of the points and your opponent has only 20, then defeating your units does not guarantee him victory in the game. If he fails to score at least 85 points at the end of the tenth round, he loses.

But that doesn't mean that you and your opponent should stand across from each other and admire each other's armies. Speaking from personal experience, battles for the central holding point are sometimes even bloodier than Harvest mode. Especially when one or both players pour clouds of poison over Hold points or force traps. 

And don't forget about the Dwarves. They lack initiative and mobility, unlike humans and elves, but they spend only one movement point (or one movement square) instead of two to occupy Hold points. At the crucial moment, this nuance can turn the tide of battle. In addition, it's a challenge to kill an upgraded Shilder or Hird warrior... And it's impossible to move him if he uses Battle Formation.

But that doesn't mean you should play Holdout exclusively with Dwarves. We've only shared with you the simplest, albeit not completely obvious, strategy. We assure you there are many more!

notes.title: Harvest Mode in Odra: Strategies, Secrets, and Survival
notes.content:
Are you already reaping the benefits of your first victories? We hope so! Today we are going to talk about some nuances of the “Harvest” mode, which we hope you have already tried out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/f4a577b055e707d8daaf7141229c62f521b9c2d1.png[/img]

Those who haven't tried it yet and don't fully understand the context, we'll bring you up to speed. Harvest is a separate game mode with different victory conditions from the classic one. If in the latter (called “Confrontation”) you just need to deprive your opponent of all units in order to win, then “Harvest” offers a special experience. In “Harvest” mode you have to gain reaping points faster than your opponent by killing as many enemy units as possible. At the same time, neutral opponents appear in the arena. We will talk about the peculiarities of their appearance.

In the “Harvest” mode, you must get harvest points faster than your opponent by killing as many enemy units as possible.

The first thing you should know about Harvest mode is that when you defeat all enemy units, you gain the upper hand just like in Confrontation (this rule, for example, does not apply to Hold, but we'll talk about it in the next posts). However, this doesn't mean that the most effective strategy is to defeat enemy units and completely ignore neutral units.

Neutral units appear on the map between opponents. The number of neutral units depends on the number of players on the map. They come at different stages of the game, which brings an element of surprise and great variety to the gameplay both at the beginning of the game and at different stages of the game. The strength of the arena units depends on its type, and this point should not be underestimated. If you have the lowest difficulty, then neutral units have the rank of “veteran”. In case you and your opponent have more pumped up warriors, earning harvest points by killing neutral units can be a priority. it is more profitable not only to kill neutral units, but also to take the points that your opponent has set up for. Be sure to try to steal a couple of kills from your opponent with a catcher or marksman!

Other types of arenas not only give units the “Champion” and “Elite” ranks, but also provoke the appearance of minibosses - unique units with increased characteristics and special mechanics (they are guaranteed to appear on the “Master” difficulty). Even with fully pumped units (rank - “Elite”), you may not be able to withstand such an onslaught. in this case, the match from hunting neutral units turns into a survival. The winner is the one who will be defeated later by neutral units.

For dessert, let's tell you a couple of hidden rules of the mode. When you get three Harvest points, you also get one point of strength, which can help you fend off the onslaught of your rival, and also help you get the remaining points to win. One more thing - the battle ends when a certain number of neutral units appear in the arena. keep a close eye on the bar at the top left of the screen.

We recommend using at least one mage or archer with AOE damage in Harvest mode (empire archers have an ability that deals such damage).

notes.title: Unite, Compete, and Conquer Together
notes.content:
Odra Online pays a lot of attention to the social component and cooperative elements. Yes, some rewards for, for example, trials of the day, you can get in games against bots. You can easily pump up your units in training battles against AI, and as the main game mode prefer Battle Pits, which is a great PvE experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/66b962a6a021b46800754584f28890777b5c59cc.jpg[/img]

But this approach deprives you of some of the content and much of the fun of mastering it. The game gives you the opportunity to fight in ranked games against players. No matter how strong the AI is, a real opponent will always find something to surprise you. And finding an ally in a pair and conquering the rating battles together with him, you will discover more than a dozen of different tactics and strategies that will help to reveal the potential of units of each of you to the maximum. 

The Battle Pits are no exception in this case. In them the “Doubles” option is available, which allows you, together with your friend, to fight back against waves of enemies and earn rating points. Battle Pits can also give a single player enough challenge and a unique gaming experience, but it hardly compares to co-op.

Add each other as friends to face your rivals shoulder to shoulder in exciting battles! And in the future we will try to please you with an in-game guild system. However, you can already gather in advance in small companies and lay the foundations of clans for the purpose of joint play.

notes.title: Factions and Classes in Odra: Choosing the Right Strategy
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/66b21151f6005dc9528979e7a06dabbc192333c6.png[/img]
As you may have already noticed, there are six different classes in the game, which are divided into three different factions.

With a simple calculation you can determine that each faction has six units of rank 1 (warrior, archer, trapper, leader, healer and mage). There are twice as many rank 2 units: two warriors, two archers, two sorcerers, and so on. 

One rank 2 unit is an ideological extension of a rank 1 unit. For example, the 1st rank Elven Slaughterer and the 2nd rank Wind Dancer are similar in concept and abilities: both have high mobility and the ability to deal splash damage (damage to multiple targets). while the 2nd rank Krongha Guardian, which has the same warrior class, is able to apply a bleed effect, hit two targets through and repel enemies (which is useful for many combinations, which will be discussed in upcoming posts).

There are currently three factions in the game: the Free Empire of Humans, the Mountain Clans of Dwarves, and the Forest Alliance of Elves and Nature Creatures. In addition to the common lore, the units of these factions have a few simple but significant features. 

Elves have increased initiative and damage, but low health and low defense. Elven spellcasters, on the other hand, prefer to deal intermittent area damage and lower the stats of enemies (using the spells “Poison Cloud” and “Raging Maze” respectively). The leader mechanic allows you to grow sacred trees for several turns, around which sectors appear, giving various bonuses to Forest Union units and making it difficult for all other units to move. There are certain conditions that must be met in order to get the bonuses, but for now let's give you a little hint - be sure to pair your Nymph with an Ent.

Dwarves of the Mountain Clans, on the other hand, have increased health and high defense. And they also ignore elevation debuffs like hold sectors, so be sure to try these stalwarts in Hold mode. Lots of control and repel/attraction skills, summon magic, aoe control, traps, mass buffs and regeneration make the Mountain Clans the most survivable and adaptive faction. Try surprising your opponent by pulling them in with the Archer's Harpoon on the Engineer's Sleeping Star. We'll tell you more about other combinations that can turn the tide of battle in the future! If you don't tell us about them in the comments.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/e370e220ea946dfa5541ee1474aa580ac9a14842.png[/img]
The Humans of the Free Empire are a cross between the two factions described above. They don't have as much health and defense as dwarves, and they have less mobility and damage than elves. They can't stand out with any of that, but at the same time they don't sag in any aspect. And the individual features and abilities of the units can give a different gaming experience from others. Human shooters, the only ones in the game at the moment, have abilities with AOE damage. Leaders and warriors, following the concept of the faction, are something between elves and dwarves (there are mobile and powerful Gladiators of rank 2 and tenacious Latniks of rank 2, as a simple example). Healers, like elves, specialize in instant healing to a single target or area. They do not impose a buff, but can apply their skills to any sector (while Elven healers need to be on a sector with Forest cover, and Dwarven healers impose buffs and regeneration on allies). Mages of the Empire have no control (with the exception of the Elementalist, a rank 2 unit), but instead are capable of unleashing many different types of AoE damage on the enemy, from the powerful one-time damage of Magical Blast to the gradually draining health of Ignition. Be sure to give this faction's dexterous players a try! Believe me, a Rank 2 Shadow will win you a ranked match almost single-handedly if you use it wisely.

Each faction has a lot of common combinations and passive features, but we will talk about them in the upcoming posts, which will be dedicated to each faction separately. We'll talk about which race uses the environment the best, how to maximize buffs with units of the same faction, and much more. 

Strategize, adapt your tactics to your opponent and win in the arenas of Odra Online!

notes.title: Game Modes in Odra: From Confrontation to Holdout
notes.content:
There are many different modes in the game that differ in various criteria. There are training battles, which you can customize to your liking and invite your friends or opponents to them. There are rating battles, where the rules are formed by the system, it also selects you worthy opponents. We should not forget about the Fighting Pits (which we will talk about separately) and Trials.

But today we will tell you about other modes: the very rules that you can customize yourself in a training battle, and which are generated by the game if you have regged the rating.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/8004d4f29180c2cf2cbf7e6af151632ebfd84ad8.png[/img]

Confrontation is the standard mode, about which there's basically nothing to say. The one who first strips the opponent (or opponents) of all units wins. Virtually all the interest here is created by you and your opponent. Of course, you can't do without surprises from the battlefield itself (places of power, traps, towers), but that's the topic of a separate post.

Harvest is perhaps the most variable of all the modes. Not only hostile AI-controlled units enter the arena every few turns (depending on the type of arena the strength of these units varies, and maybe even the appearance of bosses, but this will be the subject of a separate post), but also the number of participating players has a great influence on the game. in Harvest the one who kills the required number of units before others wins. Have you tried to win by stealing kills from your opponent with long-range units or abilities?

Holdout is the longest mode, but definitely not the most boring. It's the only mode where you don't have to deprive your opponent of units to win. Among other arena features, points of interest - the so-called hold points - will appear on the map. They are highlighted, you won't confuse them with anything. If your unit occupies one of these points at the moment of the round change, you get hold points.

By the way, did you know that moving to a holding point spends two movement points, not one? not for dwarves, though. the author of this post didn't know, so he has recorded several embarrassing defeats in this mode. We will talk about other nuances in the future.

notes.title: Arcanite in Odra: How to earn the game’s most valuable currency
notes.content:
Arcanite is an unusual-looking red-orange crystal, shimmering with streams of ancient energy. It is a valuable vessel of power, an extremely expensive mineral, which is highly valued in the vastness of the world of Odra. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45386108/e7a2e60624fba1e4fbd5bf8acefea3f4b94201d6.png[/img]

It is also the main currency of the game, about the main ways of obtaining which we will talk today. The history of arcanite and its true essence is still a secret.

One of the main ways to get arcanite is to fulfill the tests of the day, i.e. dailiks. you will never miss them, because they meet you on the main screen right after you start the game. Dailies are often simple and not only give you practically free arcanite, but also add variety to the gameplay by offering challenges in different types of battles. important point: if the description of a challenge does not specify that it should be a ranked battle, you can always beat up someone from your friends list in a training battle.

For example, when you log in to the game but haven't decided which mode you're going to play, and you see the challenge of the day, “The Last Hero! - Win any two matches with the “Confrontation” battle mode”, you will most likely make a decision right away. We in turn will try to make the challenges of the day even more interesting and diverse in the future.

The second way is a battle pass. By entering the game every day, completing challenges of the day and gaining the upper hand in ranked battles, you will accumulate experience and get additional arcanite and various bonus awards for it.

Particularly skillful players can successfully earn a lot of arcanite in the Trials mode on four different difficulties: Rookie, Veteran, Champion, and Hero. You can only get Arcanite by winning a Trial once per day. It is highly recommended that you evaluate your strengths sensibly. However, why not take a risk?

Experienced players have another source of arcanite mining: at the end of the rating season, bonus arcanite will be awarded for taking high places, among other rewards. Such a reward will definitely please those who actively succeeded in the arenas of ranking battles during the whole season.

Of course, we can not fail to mention the premium, since we are talking about in-game currency. It is not necessary for a comfortable game, but if you don't mind supporting the developers and speeding up the accumulation of arcanite - why not? Premium increases the reward for the trials of the day and adds two more to the three available. Not a bad help for active players.

We will be glad to know your opinion about the sources of arcanite mining in the comments! Thank you for your attention to this text and good luck in the arenas of the mystical city!
